title: Syria from the Saddle
summary: Albert Payson Terhune (1872–1942), later known for his books about dogs, rode through Syria and Palestine in the winter of 1893–94, at the age of twenty-one, with a dragoman named David and a small camp. From Beirût he went over the Lebanon to Damascus and the Hauran, then south by Galilee, Nazareth, and Samaria to Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Jericho, and the Dead Sea, and left from Jaffa. He tells of nights in Druze and Bedouin camps, a camp thief, a wedding, lepers, the pilgrims in Jerusalem, and Christmas at Bethlehem, with stories told by David and others on the way. The book has about sixty photographs and drawings.
